notes: MCP tool: the invoice is set to 'unpaid' (sent) before the generate-invoice job is enqueued; a crash in between leaves an invoice marked sent that is never generated or emailed. No outbox.
Same pattern as 969a4a4b: status 'unpaid' committed before the generate-invoice job.
REST router: same pattern (status 'unpaid' before the generate-invoice job).
A draft invoice is inserted before the schedule job; a leftover draft is a safe, user-visible state.
Notification job explicitly fire-and-forget (comment in source).
'App installed' email after creating the authorization code: best-effort email inside try/catch.
Polar webhook: team marked past_due, then a payment-issue email job inside try/catch (best effort; webhook redelivery covers crashes).
Stripe webhook: invoice marked paid, then a notification job (best effort).
Stripe webhook: invoice marked refunded, then a notification job (best effort).
API key created, then a 'new API key' email sent in the background on purpose (comment: 'We don't need to await this').
Bank connection and accounts are inserted before the initial-bank-setup task is triggered; a failure leaves a connection that never gets its initial sync.

The bank connection row is deleted before the delete-connection task (which revokes the provider connection) is triggered; a failure leaves the provider connection active, and the data needed to revoke it is already deleted.
Enrichment status set to 'pending' before the enrich-customer job is enqueued; a crash leaves the customer stuck in 'pending' (the catch handler does not run on a crash).

Best-effort 'app installed' email.
Application set to review-pending, then a review-request email to a fixed reviewer address. Whether pending applications are also visible elsewhere was not determined.
Manual transaction created, then an enrichment job. Enrichment is optional data; whether other jobs re-enrich was not determined.
Bank account balance/currency updated before the import-transactions job is enqueued; a failure leaves the new balance without the imported transactions.
Worker job: sync record upserted, then the attachment-sync job enqueued for the same transaction. BullMQ retries and the later 'already synced with changes' step may repair it; not determined.
The upsert (first loop) and the enqueue (second loop, for other, already-synced transactions) concern different records; the enqueue is not owed by that commit.

Recurring scheduler: the series is marked as having generated the invoice before the generate-invoice job is queued; a crash in between skips that occurrence (the next sweep sees it as generated).
Explicitly accepted in the source: 'Queue jobs AFTER transaction commits ... will be picked up by idempotency checks on retry, or can be manually processed via the dashboard.'
Auto-pause recorded, then a notification (best effort).

Scheduled-invoice job sets status 'unpaid' before queueing generate-invoice. On a retry after a crash the job returns early because the status is no longer 'scheduled' (checked by reading the processor), so the invoice is never generated or sent.
Transactions marked exported, then an emailed download link inside try/catch (best effort; the export remains available).
Tax data saved, then a non-blocking classification job inside try/catch.
Bot upload handler: the inbox item is committed and updated, then process-document is enqueued outside any retrying job; a crash leaves an inbox item that is never processed.
Match suggestion persisted, then a notification (best effort).
Match persisted, then a notification (best effort).
Reminder job enqueued before reminderSentAt is recorded; a failure in between sends a reminder that is not recorded (duplicates later). Low impact.
Schedule job created first on purpose; the processor skips invoices that are not 'scheduled', so an orphan job is harmless.
Explicit design: 'Create the new scheduled job FIRST to ensure we don't lose the job if creation fails'; stale-job checks in the processor.
